decidedBy: Essenthos, 2026-09-30, on the record of Deborah that held two women, found while the verse references only a dataset states were listed, each occurrence read against its verse by claude-opus-5-5
policy: A record is one person, and a word names the one its verse names. Strong heads Deborah once, H1683, for two women: Rebekah's nurse and the prophetess who judged Israel. The dataset gave the judge the number of the word for a bee, H1682, so the name resolved to the nurse's record alone and that record held the verses of both. Each occurrence is given to the woman its verse names.
source: Essenthos, on the record of Deborah that held two women, each occurrence read against its verse by claude-opus-5-5, 2026-09-30

rulings.why: 'Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Bethel under an oak': the verse says which Deborah she is.
'Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time': the judge, centuries after Rebekah's nurse was buried.
'A prophetess' stands in apposition to Deborah in the same clause, and is said of the judge.
'She dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim': the judge of the verse before, where Israel came up to her for judgment.
'Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh': the prophetess who summoned Barak in 4:6.
'Deborah went up with him': with Barak and his ten thousand, the same woman as in 4:9.
'Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which the LORD hath delivered Sisera into thine hand': the prophetess speaking to Barak.
'Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day': the song after the battle of chapter 4.
'Until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel': the singer of the song names herself.
'Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak': the song addresses its singer beside Barak.
'The princes of Issachar were with Deborah': the tribes that came to the battle of chapter 4.
